info.desc: Déjà Vu is the first album by the rock band Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, and the second by the trio configuration of Crosby, Stills, and Nash. It was released in March of 1970 by Atlantic Records, catalogue SD-7200. It topped the pop album chart for one week and generated three Top 40 singles: "Teach Your Children," "Our House," and "Woodstock." In 2003, the album was ranked number 148 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of the 500 greatest albums of all time. Déjà Vu was greatly anticipated after the popularity of the first CSN album and the addition of Young .

podcast.body: Released on March 11, 1970, this was the band's second album and their first with Neil Young, who only played on half of its tracks. Critics considered it "too perfect" and expressed doubts about replicating its "beautiful harmonies" live, sometimes commenting that it "just wasn't messy enough." *Rolling Stone* magazine has listed *Déjà Vu* multiple times in its "top 500 albums of all time," most recently at number 220. "Some critics felt that the second album and the first with Neil Young deja vu was just too perfect young only played on half of those tracks by the way there were doubts that these beautiful harmonies could be replicated live there were comments that it just wasn't messy enough."
